what: Hides the browser scrollbar and draws a custom one in a 20px strip at the right screen edge — bar length is screen height ÷ document height, position is the share read. While moving more than 1px, the 5px bar switches on at half width (scaleX .5) over .2s ease-out, and after .25s of stillness it fades out .35s later over .35s. Hovering the strip brings the bar to full width in .2s, pressing the strip widens it to the screen width and glides to that ratio position, and dragging the bar moves along — the thin scrollbar of smooth-scroll sites

options.idle: Seconds until it counts as stopped, default .25
options.is-scrolling · is-down: Attaches to the element while it moves · while it is held down
options.api: Global name of the smooth-scroll object (window[api].scrollTo(y, { immediate }) — Lenis etc.). If given, pressing the strip slides with that damping (original smooth strip press: the bar moves over .63s) and dragging moves it immediately. If absent, the window (or data-fx-scroller) is moved immediately

use: — html, from the consumer’s css { scrollbar-width: none } · html::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none }
note: On devices with no hover (hover false) it is not attached and the css hides it too — phone uses its own scrollbar. It only intercepts presses on the strip

from.where: index.html .px-scrollbar — original Studio smooth scroll (scrollbar: true, g-scrollbar): [data-es-scrollbar] fixed 20px from the right, thumb::after 5px · right 5px · 5px gap top and bottom. At rest it is opacity 0 scaleX(.5) all .35s ease-out .35s. While data-es-scrolling is set (moved more than 1px, 250ms debounce) it is opacity 1 scaleX(.5) .2s, and on track hover scaleX(1) .2s, with --es-thumb-color black
